data.name: mLST8
data.description: mLST8 (GbetaL) - a shared subunit of BOTH mTOR complexes. Especially required for mTORC2 to assemble and signal to Akt; largely dispensable for mTORC1.
data.description_beginner: A small building block shared by both mTOR complexes, but it matters much more for mTORC2 - without it, mTORC2 can't properly assemble and signal to Akt, while mTORC1 mostly works fine without it.

studies.title: GbetaL, a positive regulator of the rapamycin-sensitive pathway required for the nutrient-sensitive interaction between raptor and mTOR
studies.authors: Kim DH; Sarbassov DD; Ali SM; Latek RR; Guntur KVP; Erdjument-Bromage H; Tempst P; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Discovered mLST8 (GbetaL), the third core subunit that clamps onto mTOR's kinase domain and stabilizes the complex. It fine-tunes how tightly Raptor holds mTOR in response to nutrients - a small but essential cog that later turned out to be especially critical for the mTORC2 complex.

studies.title: Ablation in mice of the mTORC components raptor, rictor, or mLST8 reveals that mTORC2 is required for signaling to Akt-FOXO and PKCalpha, but not S6K1
studies.authors: Guertin DA; Stevens DM; Thoreen CC; Burds AA; Kalaany NY; Moffat J; Brown M; Fitzgerald KJ; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: The foundational genetic 'dissection' of the two complexes in living mice. Deleting Raptor was lethal early (mTORC1 essential); deleting Rictor or mLST8 selectively knocked out mTORC2 signaling to Akt and PKCalpha but spared S6K1. This cleanly assigned jobs to each complex and showed mLST8 is an mTORC2-specific requirement in mice.

relations.mechanism: mLST8 is dispensable for mTORC1 in vivo but essential for mTORC2 - a rare clean genetic separation of the two complexes.
relations.mechanism_beginner: This protein isn't needed for mTORC1 in a living animal, but mTORC2 can't work without it – a clean genetic way to tell the two complexes apart.
relations.note: The cleanest genetic argument that the two complexes are truly separate machines.
